summary: How Adolf Hitler and Erich Ludendorff tried to seize power in Munich in November 1923 by storming a beer hall, failed in a deadly street battle, and were then shielded by sympathetic police and judges who turned the trial into Nazi propaganda.

evidence.note: Hitler moves to Munich in 1913 to dodge Austrian service; start of the covered years
Bavarian council republics and their bloody suppression by the Freikorps in May 1919
Eisner assassination and retaliatory shooting open a cycle of political violence
police chief Pohner protects and aids the early Nazi movement
founding of the party by Drexler, Hitler sent in as an army spy, Eckart's influence
Eckart shapes the Hitler myth as party propaganda
stormtroopers seize the beer hall on the night of 8 November 1923
Nazis wreck a socialist newspaper and beat and kidnap Jewish residents overnight
march ends in a gun battle at a police cordon; Ludendorff's role and arrest
biased judge Neithardt and right-wing leniency of the Weimar courts
Landsberg imprisonment, writing Mein Kampf, parole in December 1924

notes: Hitler made secondary, not primary: the story covers his 1913-1924 years only, so the lifetime rule would not fit; the title names the event. January 6 2021 comparisons throughout are comparisons, so reaches_present is false. Host says the Nazi party was founded in February 1920 (DAP founded 1919, renamed 1920). No content warning: violence is described briefly, not graphically.
